title: Xanthe and the Letter
premise: In 1918, apprentice clockmaker Noor Eriksen is summoned to repair the observatory's dying master clock and finds a hidden letter from his late mentor, Xanthe Voss, exposing the names the army has erased from the town ledger. As occupying forces tighten control and the armistice nears, Noor must carry Xanthe's letter past three checkpoints to a delegate who can restore the townspeople's identities before the peace is signed without them. He succeeds at the cost of revealing himself, and the novel ends with the names read aloud in the rebuilt town square while Noor, no longer invisible, winds the repaired clock.
about_author: August Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records from occupied European towns. Their fiction explores what paperwork remembers when people are made to forget.

chapters.title: The Clock That Counted Everyone
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Summoned to the observatory, Noor repairs the master clock and discovers a letter sewn into Xanthe Voss's old workbench, naming the townspeople the army has struck from the requisitioned ledger. He hesitates, remembering which silences keep people safe. Emotional beat: the pull between inherited fear and inherited duty as the first checkpoint is announced.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The army occupies the town fully; ration cards replace names, and Noor's own apprenticeship papers are confiscated. He copies the letter's contents into cipher on clock diagrams, hiding evidence in plain sight. A soldier who once bought a watch from him recognizes him and looks away. Emotional beat: belonging tested through small mercies and growing danger.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Racing the armistice negotiations, Noor carries the diagrams toward the delegate's convoy, passing a bridge checkpoint by posing as a repairman, a rail checkpoint by hiding the pages inside a pendulum case, and finally the square checkpoint where the soldier from before stands guard. The soldier stops him. Emotional beat: climax of fear, choice, and the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Names Weigh
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The soldier, himself unnamed on the army rolls, lets him pass; the delegate reads the letter and halts the signing until the ledger is restored. After the armistice, the townspeople gather in the square as their names are read aloud, and Noor winds the master clock to mark the hour. Emotional beat: resolution through memory reclaimed and a self finally belonging to a community.
